guidance.opening:
秋日波士顿，诺特先生的办公室里纸张堆得发黄，窗缝漏进潮湿的街声。他推开一份租约，指节敲了敲桌面，抬眼打量来客。
“先说说，您是哪位，平日做什么营生？”
报个姓名、一个职业概念便够开场；或许再问一两句，随后会拟一份完整草稿供你过目。
guidance.advice: 1920s Boston hire setup: landlord Steven Knott may later engage someone by the day over a vacant house neighbors nickname the Corbitt House after the Macarios fled and some family members ended in an asylum—public rumor only; do not treat hire, keys, cash, or a written brief as already done. Occupations that fit paper trails, interviews, or a daylight look at a rental: Journalist, Librarian, Lawyer, Private Investigator, Police Detective, Police Officer, Professor, Antiquarian, Author, Parapsychologist, Doctor of Medicine, Engineer, Clergy, Dilettante. Useful training without inventing numbers: Library Use, History, Law, Fast Talk or Persuade, Spot Hidden, Listen, Psychology; Latin or Italian can help records or former tenants later. Era kit: notebook, press card or professional card, modest 1920 clothing, streetcar fare—not scenario keys or advance pay. Public involvement: Globe morgue, Hall of Records/Central Library, neighbors, former tenants, or the house itself are all listed as possible starts after identity exists. Optional ties (not facts): Boston local, acquaintance of a tenant, curiosity about haunted rentals, need of day work. Optional motivation questions only if conversation wants color. Preserve uncertainty; do not force a profession. Use the existing setup tool for the card.
guidance.handoff: The visitor is in Steven Knott's Boston office being asked who they are and what work they do. Identity is not yet settled; no commission has been accepted and no keys, cash, or other items have been received. Continue the character-creation meeting there until a draft investigator is ready for review.
